---
title: "Is there a better time in the year to buy a house in Australia?"
date: 2026-10-24
categories: [Housing Economics]
description: "I want to know whether dwelling prices in Australia are seasonal."
---

In this analysis, I explore whether there is a better time in the year to buy a house in Australia. I use data on median prices of established house transfers from the Australian Bureau of Statistics and apply time series analysis to identify any seasonal patterns in the housing market. By understanding these patterns, potential homebuyers can make more informed decisions about when to enter the market.

## Capital city house prices

```{python}
#| label: fig-capital-prices
#| echo: false

import sys

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

sys.path.insert(0, "../etl")
from housing_prices import CATALOGUE, PROCESSED_FILE, RELEASE_LABEL, TABLE

CAPITALS = [
    "Sydney", "Melbourne", "Brisbane", "Adelaide",
    "Perth", "Hobart", "Darwin", "Canberra",
]
MEASURE = "Median Price of Established House Transfers (Unstratified)"

df = pd.read_csv(PROCESSED_FILE, parse_dates=["date"])
series = (
    df.loc[(df["measure"] == MEASURE) & df["region"].isin(CAPITALS)]
      .pivot(index="date", columns="region", values="value")
)
# Order the lines by latest value so the legend reads top-down with the chart.
legend_order = series.iloc[-1].sort_values(ascending=False).index
series = series[legend_order]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
series.plot(ax=ax, linewidth=1.4)
ax.set_ylabel("Median price ($'000)")
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False, ncol=2)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax.margins(x=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

display(Markdown(
    f"*Median price of established house transfers, Australian capital cities. "
    f"Source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Total Value of Dwellings, "
    f"{RELEASE_LABEL} (cat. no. {CATALOGUE}), {TABLE}.*"
))
```
